subject: Proposal: triple-lane demo windows + DST safeguard for Finteq execs
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@finteq.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Gupta <r.gupta@paywise.co>
Date: 2027-10-28T08:12:00-04:00
Subject: Request: Exec demo across US/EU/APAC w/ DST awareness

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for taking this on. We need a single coordinated demo for three executive audiences (Finteq, PayWise, and two strategic partners) that spans US / EU / APAC calendars. The sticky bit: our CFO travels and the US switches off DST on 2027-11-07 — we want to avoid invites that accidentally shift for any exec.

Target week: Nov 8–12. Prefer all-day windows so regional teams can join relevant segments. Can your team propose concrete time slots that map to each region (with local times and UTC) plus a fallback if DST causes a one-hour drift?

High-level asks:
- Live executive Q&A for all three regions (not just recorded)
- A short recorded version for APAC if their execs can't join live
- Mutual action plan (NDA already in place) and a calendar seed we can accept/reject

Attaching a rough availability matrix from Finteq execs. cc: Rajesh for PayWise alignment.

Best,
Elena Rossi
CTO, Finteq
elena@finteq.com

Attachments: finteq_exec_avail.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finteq.com>
Cc: Rajesh Gupta <r.gupta@paywise.co>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-28T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Exec demo across US/EU/APAC w/ DST awareness

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Forwarding a quick proposal and attaching a mutual action plan + a sample .ics seed.

Proposal (three "lanes", all times are local; I've also listed UTC):
1) US lane — morning exec block: 08:30–10:00 PT (16:30–18:00 UTC)
2) EU lane — late-afternoon exec block: 15:00–16:30 CET (14:00–15:30 UTC)
3) APAC lane — morning regional block: 09:30–11:00 SGT (01:30–03:00 UTC)

DST contingency: US DST ends 2027-11-07. For any invites scheduled in the week after DST change (Nov 8+), we will send invites anchored to fixed UTC times (not local) and explicitly call out the local display time so Outlook/Gmail do not auto-adjust unexpectedly. We'll also provide a recorded backup that can be played on-demand.

Next steps: please confirm which two dates in Nov 8–12 work for your execs and whether PayWise requires their own dedicated window or can join the US/EU lanes.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx, exec_calendar_seed.ics

—
Irene Choi

On Thu, Oct 28, 2027 at 11:05 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposal (three "lanes", all times are local; I've also listed UTC):

All — small tweak: for EU we should present times in CEST for invites if we confirm earlier in the week (some participants are on CEST in early Nov before CET strictness) and for APAC double-check whether Singapore (SGT) or Japan (JST) should be the canonical label — Finteq has Tokyo-based CFO on some days.

Concrete matrix suggestion (Nov 9 preferred by our ops):
- US lane: Nov 9, 08:30–10:00 PT (15:30–17:00 MST / 16:30–18:00 UTC)
- EU lane: Nov 9, 15:00–16:30 CEST (13:00–14:30 UTC) — label as CEST in invite text if we send before the local shift
- APAC lane: Nov 10, 09:00–10:30 JST (00:00–01:30 UTC) — pushing 30m earlier to accommodate Tokyo schedule

Fallback policy: if an exec absolutely cannot join a lane, we will run a 20-minute live Q&A with them separately (hosted by Marcus) and add a 30-minute follow-up 1:1 the next day.

I'll prepare a hour-by-hour overlap map (UTC) and drop it here.

—Karthik

Irene / Karthik — this looks promising. Quick notes:
- Finteq CFO (travel) can do Nov 9 US lane but prefers the earlier end time (09:45 PT) due to a flight.
- PayWise execs (cc'd) would rather join the EU lane if possible. Rajesh, can you confirm PayWise availability on Nov 9 EU lane?
- APAC: our Tokyo lead can do Nov 10 but asks if we can start 30m earlier as Karthik suggested.

If we can lock Nov 9 (US + EU) and Nov 10 (APAC) with the slight shifts, we'll accept. Please send calendar seeds that lock UTC times and call out local display times in the body.

Thanks,
Elena
